At West Kensington Surgery we organise our services around a "total triage" system.  We ask merely that all patients first tell us briefly why they need medical advice, either by submitting an online "PATCHS" form, or by briefly telling the receptionist ( the online form is better because this is then direct information from the patient - but we appreciate some people are unable to do this so offer the phone option ). This allows us to quickly provide the most appropriate care to our patients, and avoids wasting patient time with unnecessary trips to the Surgery. The vast majority of our patients find this approach efficient and helpful, and we believe it is the best way to provide modern primary care to our patients. In fact the NHS is encouraging all GP surgeries to move to this system and has required them to do so in a new contract.

While the online consultation system PATCHS ( used by us and hundreds of practices across the UK ) was developed in collaboration with and is evaluated by the University of Manchester, the University's involvement is primarily in research and development to ensure the tool is safe, useful, and delivers maximum benefits to patients and the NHS.
